In Re:- Manik Rui Das vs Re: An Application For Bail Under ... on

Author: Ashim Kumar Roy

entities.text: Manik Rui Das vs Re: An Application For Bail
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bench: Ashim Kumar Roy 134 23.11.2016 p.d. C.R.M. No. 9281 of 2016 In re:- Manik Rui Das ... Petitioner.

-And- Re: An application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. affirmed on 24.10.2016 in connection with Moyna Police Station Case No.228/2015 dated 28.9.2015 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 read with West Bengal Act 42 of 1973 and Sections 3/304/120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 46AA of the Bengal Excise Act, 1909 and Section 16 (3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Mr. Intiaz Ahmed, Mr. Hasibul Islam .....
For the petitioner.

Mr. Manjit Singh, P.P., Mr. A. A.
Siddiqui .... For the State.
Heard the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the parties.
Perused the case diary.
It is submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioner that his client has approached this Court for bail for the first time and now he is in custody for 1 year 55 days.
He further submits that the only allegation against his client is that from his possession 6 liters of spurious I.D.liquor was recovered and by consuming the same, one person died.
Then he submits that one of the co-accused was granted bail from whose possession, 5 litres of such I.D.liquor was recovered.

On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor opposes the prayer for bail and submits that this is case, where by consuming the spurious I.D.liquor, total 23 persons died and according to the materials collected during investigation, it appears that the petitioner is not only the seller but he is the kingpin, who sold those spurious I.D.liquor to other accused and from whose shop after purchasing and by consuming such I.D.liquor, they died.
Then he points out that already trial has commenced and out 77 witnesses, the examination of 8 witnesses is complete and the delay in commencement of the trial is not for the prosecution.
Now, considering the rival submissions of the parties and the materials available from the case diary, we are of the opinion that this is not a fit case for bail.
Accordingly, the application for bail stands rejected.

However, we direct the learned court below once again to proceed with the trial with utmost expedition and to conclude the same as expeditiously as possible, preferably within six months from the date of communication of this order.
